s: object (that around which an emotion or activity centers)
asset, property (something of high value, especially real estate)
Objekt.et: From Middle High German object (14th c.), from Latin obiectum.

s: genitive singular of Object Request Broker

Objektiv.et: Since the first half of the 19th century, originally a clipping of Objektivglas (since the 18th century). Compare also French objectif and verre objectif.
